newsitem.title: UK: SAfrica sees GDP up 2.5%, rate policy "wait & see".
newsitem.headline: SAfrica sees GDP up 2.5%, rate policy "wait & see".

text.p: South African finance minister Trevor Manuel said on Monday he expected gross domestic product to meet government estimates of 2.5 percent this year.

At the same time, James Cross, deputy governor of the South African Reserve Bank, said at a conference here that the central bank's policy on interest rates was still to "wait and see" awaiting developments on inflation.
Manuel said the anticipation was that "this year will be a year of consolidation". He added, "We've done the bulk of our work for GDP estimates of 2.5 percent."
When asked at a news conference whether South Africa would meet the 2.5 percent target for GDP he said yes.

Cross said, "We will have to open our economy to outward flows, otherwise we will suffer...as far as monetary policy is concerned. As far as interest rates are concerned, it is still a wait and see issue.
"We need to wait and see the developments that will take place on the inflation front and the money creation front."
-- Diane Craft in Edinburgh, London newsroom +44 171 542 6784
